summary: Both editions were independently checked against all seven paragraphs of the selected Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Each preserves the destruction clause’s necessity, the bracketed dwelling phrase, selected pronoun number, direct second-person purification, complete purity and usefulness clauses, negative command, conditional nothing formulation, and distinction between the noise and the narrator’s fearful inference. The notes accurately disclose the supplied reports’ relevant alternatives and distinguish editorial brackets, corrections, and supplied wording from first-hand text. The simplified edition’s shorter sentences preserve these source claims independently of the standard. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to the supplied working source and disclosure of the supplied evidence; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify the cited editions, or establish an exhaustive collation.
